claims.text: The Pulumi `protect` resource option is a Pulumi-engine construct that is enforced entirely within Pulumi.
The Pulumi `protect` resource option is never sent to the cloud provider.
Many cloud resources carry their own deletion-protection attributes separate from Pulumi's `protect` option, such as `deletionProtection` on a GCP Cloud SQL instance.
AWS RDS instances have a `deletionProtection` attribute (deletion protection) separate from Pulumi's `protect` option.
Cloud-provider deletion-protection attributes (e.g., `deletionProtection` on GCP Cloud SQL or AWS RDS) are enforced by the cloud provider independently of anything Pulumi knows about.
A resource can be unprotected in Pulumi (`protect` false) and still refuse to delete due to provider-side deletion protection, or be protected in Pulumi yet deletable at the provider level.

The page /docs/iac/operations/troubleshooting/destroy-failures/ has a section 'Deletion protection on the resource itself' explaining how to tell Pulumi protect and provider deletion protection apart and resolve each.
Many cloud resources carry their own deletion-protection attributes, separate from Pulumi's `protect` resource option, that the provider or the cloud API enforces independently.
A GCP Cloud SQL instance (Pulumi `gcp.sql.DatabaseInstance`) has a `deletionProtection` attribute that provides deletion protection independent of Pulumi's `protect` option.
An AWS RDS instance (Pulumi `aws.rds.Instance`) has a `deletionProtection` attribute that provides deletion protection independent of Pulumi's `protect` option.
Pulumi's `protect` resource option and a cloud resource's own deletion-protection attributes are complementary rather than substitutes for one another.

The Pulumi docs page 'Destroy failures' at /docs/iac/operations/troubleshooting/destroy-failures/ has a section 'Deletion protection on the resource itself' explaining how to tell `protect` and resource-level deletion protection apart and resolve a destroy failure caused by either.

Pulumi has no single flag to protect every resource in a stack; stack transforms can set `protect: true` on every resource as it is registered, documented at /docs/iac/concepts/resources/options/transforms/#stack-transforms.
Pulumi's `protect` resource option is an engine-level guard that never reaches the cloud provider.
When `pulumi destroy` fails because of the `protect` resource option, the error message names a URN and mentions `protect`.
The page /docs/iac/concepts/resources/options/protect/ exists and explains how to remove the `protect` option.

Some Pulumi providers refuse to issue the delete call when a resource carries a deletion-protection attribute, e.g. `deletionProtection` on `gcp.sql.DatabaseInstance` and `gcp.container.Cluster`; the failure surfaces from the provider before any request reaches the cloud API.
`gcp.sql.DatabaseInstance` and `gcp.container.Cluster` have a `deletionProtection` attribute.

AWS RDS `deletionProtection`, EC2 `disableApiTermination`, and Azure Resource Manager management locks are protections enforced by the cloud API itself, rejecting the delete call independent of Pulumi.
Cloud-API-enforced deletion protection errors come back from the cloud provider's API, often with a distinct error code such as `ScopeLocked` (Azure management lock).
`pulumi destroy` deletes what is recorded in the stack's state, not what the program currently says.

For provider-enforced and cloud-API-enforced deletion protection, setting the attribute to false in the program alone is not enough; you must set it to false, run `pulumi up` so the change reaches the live resource and state, then run `pulumi destroy`.

If deletion protection was already disabled outside Pulumi (e.g., in the cloud console), `pulumi refresh` synchronizes state with reality and `pulumi destroy` then succeeds without an intervening `pulumi up`.
`gcp.sql.DatabaseInstance` has a nested `settings.deletionProtectionEnabled` attribute that also guards the instance at the GCP API level, in addition to the provider-enforced `deletionProtection`.
`gcp.bigquery.Table` has a provider-enforced `deletionProtection` attribute.
`gcp.bigquery.Dataset` has a `deleteContentsOnDestroy` attribute; destroying a dataset that still contains tables fails unless it is `true`.
`aws.rds.Instance` and `aws.rds.Cluster` have a `deletionProtection` attribute that is enforced by the AWS API and defaults to `false`.
`aws.s3.BucketV2` has a `forceDestroy` attribute that defaults to `false`; a non-empty bucket otherwise fails to delete.
`aws.ec2.Instance` has a `disableApiTermination` attribute enforced by the AWS API (EC2 termination protection).
`aws.dynamodb.Table` has a `deletionProtectionEnabled` attribute enforced by the AWS API that defaults to `false`.
`azure-native.authorization.ManagementLockByScope` and scope-specific variants such as `ManagementLockAtResourceLevel` exist in the Pulumi Azure Native provider for management locks.
Azure Resource Manager enforces management locks: a `CanNotDelete` lock must be removed before the resource can be deleted, independent of the Pulumi program.

Destroying an `azure-native.keyvault.Vault` only soft-deletes it; recreating a vault with the same name fails with `VaultAlreadyExists` until the soft-deleted vault is purged or recovered, and purge protection prevents purging until its retention period elapses.
